name: Tombstone

debutSeason.notes: Name first used on a 340 lb superheavyweight that won the 2004 BattleBots NPC Charity Open (beat The Judge twice). A 220 lb heavyweight Tombstone finished 4th at the untelevised 2009 Pro Championship. The heavyweight is a descendant of Ray Billings' Last Rites; design inspired by Comedy Central-era M.O.E. but with two wheels. Competed WC I-VI; withdrew from WC VII (2022) while Ray recovered from hand surgery.

weaponDescription: Huge full-width horizontal bar spinner mounted at the front of a tubular weapon support, spinning just above the floor. Bar weighs 65-75 lb normally (its shortest/heaviest bar, used vs Brutus in 2016, was close to 80 lb). Ray brings an arsenal of interchangeable bars: silver, black and solid red bars in 2015; the red S7-steel bar repainted blue for the 2016 title run; a 2 in thick 71 lb bar in 2018; gray titanium bar with AR500 steel teeth, black S7 tool steel bar, red S7 bar (2019); H13 tool steel and I-shaped AR500 bars (2020); ten bars in total by 2020. Driven by an exposed chain from a big brushed motor, the chain being a known weak point (Bombshell targeted it in 2016 and it came off vs Bombshell in 2018). Rule change in 2018 capped tip speed at 250 mph, so Tombstone was tuned down to about 200 mph. For the 2026 Pro League the single brushed weapon motor was replaced by three brushless motors.

weaponSpecs.motor: Etek ME0708 brushed motor (heavyweight build); three brushless motors from 2026
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb is the top of the wiki's stated 65-75 lb range (one bar ~80 lb). tipSpeedMph 200 = the 2018 de-tune to meet the 250 mph limit; the broadcast quoted 235 mph for its 71 lb bar vs Gigabyte (2018). Pre-2018 bars exceeded 250 mph (exact figure not given). teethOrImpactors=2 refers to the two ends of the bar.

drive.selfRighting: none (invertible)
drive.motors: NPC T64 originally; Magmotors with Whyachi gearboxes from 2022; 2x Maytech 8085 brushless outrunners (2026)

armor.chassisShape: Low, box-shaped welded tube frame. The front 'nose' tapers in to the weapon support with armor across it from 2016. Large exposed tires sit outside the frame at the back corners and act as bait. Frame got shorter and lower over the years (3 in shorter and 1 in lower in 2021).

appearance.features: Flat, low rectangular body, much narrower than the bar. A long horizontal bar (wider than the robot) spins flat across the front at low height, mounted on a short tubular nose. Two big black rubber tires stick out of the sides at the rear and are clearly visible from above; no wheel guards until the 2026 build. 2015-2018: gray/silver steel side panels with the word TOMBSTONE cut into the top armor plate, usually a red bar (2015) or blue bar (2016 title run). 2019 onward: all black, with a grim reaper logo sticker and a TOMBSTONE name sticker on the top plate and vent cut-outs; usually a black or gray bar. The weapon drive chain is visible at the front. Spins clockwise or counter-clockwise depending on setup; the robot can drive upside down.

otherAwards: Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship I, 2015)
Successful Bounty defense vs Gruff (BattleBots: Bounty Hunters)
2004 NPC Charity Open superheavyweight champion
notableRecords: Only BattleBots robot to win championships as both a superheavyweight and a heavyweight
Only #1 seed to win the Giant Nut without being the defending champion
Reached the first two reboot finals (2015, 2016)
Competitive record 33-17 (wiki, through 2026 Pro League)

famousFights.summary: Championship final. Bombshell went for Tombstone's exposed weapon chain and missed. Tombstone's blue bar then ripped Bombshell's front tires off and knocked it out cold within seconds, and kept tearing into its frame until the count-out. Tombstone won its first Giant Nut.

Championship final. Bite Force scooped and pinned Tombstone against the rails. Tombstone's batteries overheated and caught fire (white smoke) so its weapon lost speed. Both robots were struggling by the final buzzer.
Main Event. End Game hit Tombstone's right wheel, Tombstone's tire jammed against the screws, and End Game punted the former champ out of the arena.
famousFights.result: Lost by KO (0:39, out of the arena)

trivia: The name comes from the computer-networking term 'tombstoning': killing something so it stays dead.

name: Bite Force

debutSeason.notes: Paul Ventimiglia previously won the 2009 BattleBots heavyweight title with Brutality. Bite Force got in as an alternate for 2015 and was built in a hurry after the team learned nine days before filming that it had been selected. Its working name was 'Chompy'. Competed WC I-IV plus the 2019 re:MARS all:STARS event. Withdrew from WC V (COVID) and has been on hiatus since.

weaponDescription: 2015: a tracked grappler/lifter with lifting forks and a clamping upper jaw. The jaw could be swapped for a heavy steel plow (cobalt-blue or black) against spinners, and magnets on the tracks improved grip. 2016-2019: completely redesigned as a 4WD robot with an asymmetric vertical bar spinner centered at the front, powered by a Motenergy ME0909 in 2016. Midway through 2018 (after the End Game fight) it switched to four S28-150 Magmotors, running the whole robot at 24 V. Front configurations were swapped by opponent: four small hinged blue wedgelets as standard, a wide blue anti-spinner plow, or a heavy steel wedge. UHMW chain guards were added in 2018 after Chomp knocked off its weapon chain in 2016.

weaponSpecs.notes: 40 lb bar refers to the 2018 title-winning version. RPM, tip speed and bar length were not found in the wiki or on battlebots.com.

drive.motors: 2x S28-400 Magmotors (9 hp) driving homemade urethane wheels (spinner version); 2015 version used tracks

materials: aluminum chassis with interlocking welded joints (2016+)
armor.chassisShape: Spinner version: very low, wide, short wedge-shaped 4WD body with the bar spinner set into the center of the front between wedgelets. Triangular construction on the side panels. Nearly all offense and defense is at the front.

appearance.features: Spinner version (2016-2019, the three-time-champion look): a squat, wide, flat body in bare aluminum, low to the floor, with four wheels mostly tucked inside the body. A thick vertical bar spinner sits in a slot in the middle of the front, with its axle running side to side. Four small hinged wedgelets (blue) scrape the floor in front of it, or one wide blue anti-spinner plow. The side panels have a triangular structure, and sponsor decals cover the top and back panels. It kept visible battle scars from season to season. 2015 grappler version: tracked box with black treads, a blue lifting fork/jaw at the front and an upper clamping jaw.

otherAwards: Won the 2016 exhibition rumble vs Witch Doctor and Wrecks
notableRecords: 26-1 competitive record: best of the reboot era
Only loss: Chomp by JD (World Championship II, 2016)
Never knocked out
19-fight win streak, the longest in show history
Only reboot-era repeat Giant Nut winner (three titles)
Only tracked robot and only non-spinner to win a reboot Giant Nut (2015)
Went a perfect 8-0 in 2018 and 8-0 in 2019

famousFights.summary: Final. Bite Force charged to keep Tombstone's bar from spinning up, scooped it and pinned it on the rails. Tombstone's batteries caught fire, and Bite Force pushed it around despite drive trouble of its own.

Final. Minotaur launched Bite Force and knocked a wedgelet off, but its drum stopped for good after one exchange. Bite Force hit Minotaur's exposed wheel and pushed it to the screws for the count-out.
Semi-final rematch. On the second hit Bite Force sheared off about a third of Tombstone's bar and tore off a wheel, leaving Tombstone shaking itself apart until it was counted out.
Chomp's first hammer swing knocked Bite Force's weapon chain off within five seconds. Bite Force fought on as a pusher but backed over its own chain and got stuck. This was its only career loss.

trivia: The name comes from the 'bite force quotient' scientists use to compare animal jaw strength.

name: Witch Doctor
team: Team Witch Doctor (formerly Busted Nuts Robotics)

debutSeason.notes: A 120 lb middleweight Witch Doctor (built by Adam Bercu) won BotsIQ 2010 and 2011 before the heavyweight was built. Has competed in every World Championship.

weaponDescription: Front vertical spinner. 2015: a single asymmetric disk. From 2016: a double-sided disk. 2018: a 47 lb two-tooth weapon at about 4000 rpm / 200 mph. Through the middle years it mostly ran the wider 'drisk' (a drum/disk hybrid). From 2021 it used twin weapon motors, belts outside the disks and AR500 steel. Late in 2021 it debuted a 45 lb single-tooth steel disk, which became its preferred weapon because it is lighter and spins up faster. 2022 build: brushless, about 25% faster, spinning at the 250 mph tip-speed maximum. Also carries a flamethrower. In the early seasons it ran with a 30 lb flame-throwing wedge minibot called Shaman, retired in 2018 to save weight. Front ends switch between small wedges/forks and a big steel anti-spinner plow.

weaponSpecs.motor: Twin weapon motors from 2021; brushless from 2022
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb/rpm/tipSpeed/teeth are the World Championship III (2018) figures. 2021 single disk: 45 lb, one tooth. 2022 (WC VII): 250 mph (rpm not stated).

drive.selfRighting: Hinged 'ribcage' self-righting arm on top (from 2016; near-180 degree range from 2021). 'Bunny ears' added in 2021 let it drive and keep the weapon spinning while upside down.
drive.motors: 2x long Magmotors; brushless parts tested and added for 2022

armor.chassisShape: Compact 4WD wedge-fronted box. The vertical disk sits in the center of the front between small wedges or a full plow, with a bone/ribcage-styled self-righting cage across the top. Chassis lengthened slightly in 2021 for the new weapon motor setup.

appearance.features: Purple and lime-green voodoo theme. Low 4WD body with four black tires. A vertical disk (or the wider two-disk drisk) sits in a front slot with angled front wedges or a plow, which from 2019 bends out to cover the front wheels. On top is a skeletal ribcage self-righter that hinges up from the back. It gained 'cracks' painted across the ribs in 2019 and a convex, realistic bone-style ribcage for FaceOffs 2024. A tiny homage to the Shaman minibot sits on the self-righter (2019). A flamethrower nozzle is mounted on the robot. Early versions brought Shaman, a small wedge minibot with a painted face.

otherAwards: re:MARS all:STARS BattleBots Challenge 2019 winner
Successful Bounty defense vs SubZero (BattleBots: Bounty Hunters)
Sin City Slugfest winner (BattleBots: Champions I)
Giant Washer (BattleBots FaceOffs)
BotsIQ 2010 and 2011 middleweight wins
notableRecords: Only robot to qualify for all seven World Championship tournaments
Only reboot robot to finish runner-up twice
27-second KO of ROTATOR was the fastest win of World Championship II

famousFights.summary: Quarter-final, one of the most controversial fights in show history. Both robots got stuck or crippled near the Upper Deck. The referees ordered an unstick for Witch Doctor, then never started a count on the one-wheeled Minotaur, which kept gyro-dancing. Witch Doctor circled without engaging for most of the last 90 seconds. The crowd booed the decision, and BattleBots later said it would review its 'controlled movement' rules.
famousFights.result: Won by JD (unanimous, all three judges scored it 6-5)

famousFights.summary: Final. Witch Doctor tore off Bite Force's wedgelets early, then its weapon died and one side of its drive failed. Bite Force flipped it upside down against the arena wall where the self-righter couldn't work.
Qualifier. With Shaman left out to save weight, Witch Doctor penned ROTATOR in a corner, ripped a tire off and flipped it. This was the fastest win of the season.

trivia: Captain Andrea Gellatly wrote the BattleBots alphabet book 'B is for BattleBots'.

name: Minotaur

debutSeason.notes: First Brazilian BattleBot. A new 2016 build based on RioBotz's Touro Maximus (RoboGames winner). Skipped WC V (2020) because of COVID travel restrictions.

weaponDescription: Wide, heavy steel drum spinner across the full front, 60-70 lb depending on configuration and driven by two Scorpion outrunner motors. 12,000 rpm in 2016, cut to 11,000 rpm for the 250 mph limit (2018), 9,000 rpm with bigger teeth (2019), and about 8,000 rpm / 220 mph with a heavier drum (2021-2022). Interchangeable wedges, wedgelets ('scoops') and hinged forks feed opponents into the drum. The drum's gyroscopic force lets Minotaur 'gyro-dance' and flip itself back over.

weaponSpecs.notes: massLb 70 and rpm 12,000 are Marco Meggiolaro's 2016 quote ('a 70lb drum that spins at 12,000rpm'). Later: 11,000 rpm (2018), 9,000 rpm (2019), 8,000 rpm / 220 mph (2022; 220 mph also quoted for 2021). Drum diameter not found.

drive.selfRighting: Gyroscopic self-righting with the spinning drum; it can also drive inverted (drum then spins the wrong way)
drive.motors: Brushed drive motors (still brushed in 2026)

materials: 6061-T6 aluminum chassis CNC-machined from an 8 in block
armor.chassisShape: Compact, short and wide 2-wheeled body: the drum takes up the whole front, the two wheels sit in angled side wheel guards behind it, and the sides angle slightly. Edgier profile and larger drive wheels from 2019. Thicker top panel added for 2022 against hammer saws.

appearance.features: Short, wide, dark body dominated by a big horizontal-axis drum across the whole front, with gold/bronze-colored teeth. In 2016 the drum was not yet the bronze color; it turned bronze from 2018. The two drive wheels are mostly hidden behind angled side armor/wheel guards. A detailed bull graphic covers the top panel. In 2016 it had red LED 'eyes' and a blue interior glow (both removed in 2018). Small wedgelets or long forks stick out under/beside the drum. Sponsor logos on the top and rear from 2021, including on the drum.

otherAwards: Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship II, 2016)
Giant Washer (BattleBots Proving Ground All Star Week, 2024)
notableRecords: Reached at least the quarter-finals in every World Championship it entered
No.1 seed for the World Championship VII (2022) bracket after going 4-0
Driver Daniel Freitas is widely rated by fans and builders as one of the best drivers in BattleBots

famousFights.summary: Round of 16. Minotaur's uppercut ripped off Warhead's spinning disk and dome and sent it bouncing across the BattleBox ('Warhead has been decapitated!'). It then stripped Warhead's side panels until it was counted out.
Final. Minotaur launched Bite Force and knocked off a wedgelet, but lost a wheel guard and its drum would not power back up. Bite Force picked at its exposed wheel until it stopped moving.

Round of 16 vs the defending champion and No.1 seed. Minotaur flipped End Game, broke off both of its long forks and chewed its underside in the closing seconds, guaranteeing a brand-new Giant Nut winner.

trivia: RioBotz's drum bots are bull-themed: 'Touro' is Portuguese for 'bull'.

name: HyperShock

others: Alex Bales (drove at re:MARS 2022 and Champions II)

debutSeason.notes: Built by former Ransom Everglades Robotics (high school) members. One of only four robots to compete in every reboot season. Completely rebuilt almost every season.

weaponDescription: Front vertical spinner. 2015: a 'drisk' (drum sandwiched between two disks) plus two hydraulic clamping arms on a carbon-fiber frame. 2016: claws replaced by a feeder wedge and lifting arms with swappable attachments, including the famous $12 garden rake. 2018 onward: redesigned weapon with more bite. From 2021 there are single- and double-disk options on twin weapon motors with a chain drive and a magnesium hub. 2021 single disk: an S7 steel disk sandwiched between AR500 disks, 2 in thick in total; 2021 double disk: two 1-1/4 in S7 disks. 2022: a single 2.5 in thick S7 disk (39.7 lb), or dual disks at 40 lb (1 in) or 46 lb (1-1/4 in). 'Horns' above the weapon let it keep fighting upside down.

weaponSpecs.notes: 39.7 lb = the 2022 (World Championship VII) single S7 disk, 2.5 in thick. Dual-disk options are 40 lb and 46 lb. RPM and diameter not found.

drive.selfRighting: Self-righter dropped in 2021 to save about 40 lb. Runs inverted using the horns above the disk and flips back over with the weapon's gyroscopic force.
drive.motors: 2x NeuMotor 8038 (Revolt brushless in 2019)

armor.chassisShape: Long, narrow, low 'race car' chassis (from 2021), with a wheelbase like a high-performance race car. The disk sits at the nose with forks/wedges beneath it.

appearance.features: From 2018: a neon/highlighter-yellow race-car look ('an RC car on steroids'). The 2021-2022 build has a long, narrow, sleek body with four exposed race-style tires on the corners, with 'HyperShock' printed on the sidewalls. A vertical disk (or twin disks) sits at the front nose between floor-scraping forks. Two horn-like prongs rise above the weapon so it can fight upside down. A QR code on the underside linked to a secret merch store. The 2015-2016 versions were black and silver; the 2015 version had black wheels with lime outlines and sharp ears above the weapon.

otherAwards: Best Driver Award, Will Bales (World Championship II, 2016)
Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship VI, 2021)
re:MARS all:STARS BattleBots Challenge 2022 winner (beat Tombstone, Blip, Hydra)
Sin City Slugfest I winner (BattleBots: Champions I)
notableRecords: Fastest KO in the reboot: threw Skorpios out of the arena in 24 seconds (BattleBots: Champions I)
Only robot to win Most Destructive and have its team win Best Driver
Career-best World Championship finish: Round of 16

famousFights.summary: 'The Rakening'. HyperShock bolted a $12 hardware-store rake to its self-righter, swatted Warrior Clan's flying drone (Warrior Dragon) out of the air, pinned it with the rake and smashed it, then knocked out the main robot too. Ranked No.1 on BattleBots: Most Outrageous Moments.
Golden Bolt quarter-final. Its forks got under Skorpios and three hits later it flew out of the arena: the fastest KO of the reboot.
famousFights.result: Won by KO (0:24, out of the arena)

famousFights.summary: Main Event. Went weapon-to-weapon, tore off Lock-Jaw's wheels, flipped it twice, then hit its rear plow and threw it clean over the arena wall.
famousFights.result: Won by KO (out of the arena)

trivia: The 2018 HyperShock was sold and repainted blue as 'Drift King' for Robot Ruckus 2021.

name: End Game

debutSeason.notes: First BattleBots competitor from New Zealand. Evolved from the team's heavyweight Death Toll, which won China's FMB (Fighting My Bots) in 2017-18. Missed the Top 16 in 2018 and 2019 before winning it all in 2020.

weaponDescription: Powerful vertical spinner centered in a boxy 4WD frame, reaching more than 6000 rpm in under five seconds. It started with a single-toothed disk, later interchangeable with an asymmetric bar and a teardrop-shaped disk. 2021: eight disks carried for the season. 2022: disks from 40 to 55 lb and a reversible weapon. The front end swaps between forks (including very long hinged and barbed forks), wedgelets and a 2022 'piano key' set of up to nine wedgelets, the first on a vertical spinner. Magnets (from 2021) counter gyroscopic forces and add traction.

weaponSpecs.notes: rpm and spin-up are the wiki's 'upwards of 6000rpm in under five seconds' (treat as approximate). massLb = the heaviest of the 2022 disks (range 40-55 lb). teethOrImpactors=1 for the classic single-tooth disk.

drive.selfRighting: Separate self-righting arm (2019 version styled like a pair of sunglasses over the weapon; later a single arm on the left of the weapon, fern-shaped by 2022). The weapon can also flip it back over.
drive.motors: 4x 6374 192kV brushless motors

armor.chassisShape: Boxy, compact, low 4WD box with the disk in a slot in the center front, flanked by swappable forks/wedgelets on orange mounting plates. The 2019 wedge was split down the middle and bent out past the sides.

appearance.features: Compact rectangular box with a vertical disk in the middle of the front and a row of orange forks/wedgelets under it. The long outer forks (2021) can double the robot's length. Wheels are hidden inside the box. The self-righter arm sits on top, left of the weapon: sunglasses-shaped 'shades' in 2019, fern-shaped later. Look by season: 2018 matte black with four orange fins and a solid wedge; 2019 silver chassis with a yellow stripe and big black END GAME lettering on the wedge, plus a 'Kill Count' sticker by the weapon; 2020 sponsor logos, a New Zealand flag and a silver fern on top; 2021 white top panel with a honeycomb border and sponsor logos (MaxAmps, University of Auckland). Orange is the team's accent color throughout.

otherAwards: Golden Bolt (BattleBots: Champions I, 2021)
Golden Bolt (BattleBots: Champions II, 2022)
Chris Rose Average Wrench (BattleBots Pro League 2026)
notableRecords: First international team to win the Giant Nut in the reboot (New Zealand)
Only robot to beat three different World Champions (Tombstone, Tantrum, SawBlaze)
Won its Giant Nut final by throwing Whiplash out of the arena
29-second ring-out of SawBlaze (2021), one of the shortest fights in BattleBots history
Lost at least once in every World Championship season, including the one it won

famousFights.summary: Final. End Game uppercut Whiplash's lifter, flipped it twice and bent the arm, then sent it over the wall and out of the BattleBox to become the first international reboot champion.
famousFights.result: Won by KO (out of the arena)

famousFights.summary: Main Event two years after End Game first called out Ray Billings. After a weapon-to-weapon clash Tombstone's tire stuck on the screws, and End Game launched it out of the arena.
famousFights.result: Won by KO (0:39, out of the arena)

famousFights.summary: Golden Bolt final. End Game's forks got under Witch Doctor and tossed it into the short corner. It controlled Witch Doctor into the screws until it was no longer mobile, winning the first Golden Bolt.

trivia: The space in 'End Game' was an accident on the application form; the team later linked it to the Taylor Swift song of the same name.

name: SawBlaze

debutSeason.notes: No classic-era SawBlaze. Jamison Go was on Team JACD (Overhaul) in World Championship I before starting his own team. Competed in every season WC II through WC VII, plus BattleBots: Champions II.

weaponDescription: Wedge/fork robot that slides under opponents, pins them, then swings a powered overhead arm down onto them with a spinning blade at its tip. WC II: thin circular cutting saw only (it bent and jammed vs Razorback). WC III: diamond-edged cutting disk, faster and stronger arm that doubles as the self-righter. WC IV on: interchangeable heavy asymmetric 'hammer saw' (spins downward, hits like a hammer) or a diamond abrasive cutting blade, picked per opponent. WC V: faster spin-up and spin-down. WC VI: new arm gearbox (designed with Jake Chesin) and a center fork split down the middle. WC VII: AR600 steel hammer-saw blade, Brazil wheels. Front-mounted flamethrower that burns green in later seasons (it barely worked in early fights).

weaponSpecs.notes: 5000 RPM comes from a Xometry case study that doesn't name the season. Xometry says the blades are AR steel on titanium blade shafts; the WC VII blade was AR600 (wiki). The '100lb pulverizer' in fight write-ups is the arena hazard, not SawBlaze's weapon. Belts drove the blade in WC IV (they tangled vs Blacksmith).

drive.selfRighting: overhead weapon arm swings over to push the robot upright
drive.motors: 2x T&P brushless (2x NPC Black Max in WC III)

armor.chassisShape: Low, flat wedge with a row of front forks/prongs (spring-loaded fingers) and a long weapon arm on top. The front section takes nearly a third of the weight allowance (Xometry).

appearance.features: Low black wedge chassis with bright lime-green panels and trim (the commentators call it 'the black and green robot'). Front edge: three ground-scraping steel forks/prongs (WC VI on, the center fork is split in two), which slide under opponents. A long boxy arm runs front to back along the top centerline, hinged near the rear; at its front tip is the blade (a solid, chunky asymmetric hammer-saw disk, or a thin circular saw), spinning in a vertical plane and slamming down just behind the forks. A small flamethrower nozzle points forward at the front and shoots green flame. Two large drive wheels on the sides, partly exposed (black Brazil-style rubber with white UHMW side guards in WC VII). WC II-III: small stylised dragon heads on either side of the blade (dropped from WC IV). Keep the overall shape low and long; the arm is the tallest part.

runnerUp.event: BattleBots: Champions II Golden Bolt (lost the final to End Game by split JD)

otherAwards: Founder's Award (World Championship VI)
Combat Robot Hall of Fame: honorable mention 2023, inducted 2025 (shared with Jamison Go's 30lb MegatRON)
notableRecords: Won the Giant Nut as the #8 seed, beating the #1 seed (Minotaur) on the way
First hammer-saw robot and first flamethrower robot to win the Giant Nut
10-2 across WC VII + Champions II, the most wins in one year
Matched or beat its previous finish every season: qualifiers → Top 16 → QF → QF → SF → champion
Wiki competitive record: 29-11

famousFights.summary: In the Giant Nut final against the unbeaten HUGE, SawBlaze stayed low, kept pinning and pounding HUGE against the walls with the hammer saw, and handed HUGE its first loss of the season.
Quarter-final against the #1 seed. SawBlaze lost its weapon and took massive drum hits, but trapped Minotaur against the screws until RioBotz's bot sat immobile and on fire.
The season's first fight. SawBlaze kept getting under Whiplash, shoved it into the screws and walls, then pinned it and hammered its top. Whiplash went on to finish runner-up that season.

trivia: Early builds filled the tires with pool noodles.

name: Whiplash

debutSeason.notes: Successor to the Vasquez family's Splatter (WC I 2015 and WC II 2016) and built on Splatter's blueprint. battlebots.com lists Jeff Vasquez as builder; Matt Vasquez is captain and driver.

weaponDescription: Rear-hinged lifting arm with a vertical spinning disk (about 22lb) at its front end. The arm swings 180 degrees, so it can lift, hit from overhead like a hammer saw, and self-right. Forks/wedgelets at the front can be swapped for hinged forks of different lengths. Against some opponents the disk is removed and replaced with an AR500 plate and extra armor; it ran disk-less for all of WC VI. WC IV: new, more destructive disk. WC V: new disk, bigger protected lifter gear, Brazil wheels. WC VII: all-brushless drive saved enough weight to run disk and armor together.

weaponSpecs.notes: 22lb disk mass is from the wiki and doesn't say which season. Disk size, RPM and lifter motor aren't published in the sources checked.

drive.selfRighting: lifter/weapon arm
drive.motors: 2x Mini Magmotors (WC IV on; 2x 48v AmpFlow in WC III); all-brushless by WC VII

armor.chassisShape: Low rectangular box with the lifting arm across the top; sloped front armor added later.

appearance.features: Low, wide rectangular body with four exposed black wheels (fat vulcanized-rubber Brazil wheels from WC V). A big flat lifting arm covers most of the top deck, hinged at the back; its front end drops between two front wedgelets/forks and carries a vertical spinning disk at the tip, sitting just behind the forks. The arm can flip all the way over the back. Electric yellow (#D0FF00) panels and arm with black details from WC IV on (Meggitt sponsor colours). WC III was red. Plow-only configs replace the disk with a flat steel plate on the arm.

otherAwards: Best Driver Award, WC III (Twitter poll)
Sin City Slugfest II winner (BattleBots: Champions II)
notableRecords: Made at least the Round of 16 in every season
Record 10 Main Events
First robot to flip Hydra and make it self-right (WC V)
One of three robots (with Minotaur and Witch Doctor) to have fought all five World Champions
Wiki record: 28-14

famousFights.summary: Quarter-final against the #1 seed. Whiplash flipped Hydra, the first robot ever to do so, and tore a panel off its rear in the final seconds while smoking itself.
Rookie Whiplash out-drove the #2 seed, pushing and lifting Bronco and denying it room to flip. Bronco's drive electrics gave out.
Giant Nut final. End Game flipped Whiplash twice, bending its arm so it wouldn't retract, then threw it over the wall and out of the BattleBox.
famousFights.result: Lost by KO (out of the arena)

trivia: When Tombstone ripped Whiplash in half in WC III, Chris Rose said it was in two parts: 'Whip and Lash'.
weaponTypeNote: Vertical spinning disk mounted at the tip of a 180-degree lifting/self-righting arm; classify as a spinner on a lifter arm.

name: Lock-Jaw

debutSeason.notes: Donald Hutson built Comedy Central-era Diesector, Root Canal, Tazbot and others. Lock-Jaw has fought in every reboot World Championship (I-VII).

weaponDescription: WC I-II: titanium grabbing jaws (280 degrees of rotation) plus downward-firing twin flamethrowers; WC II jaws could also act as a spring flipper, and it was rebuilt smaller on 4 wheels instead of 6. WC III on: modular robot with a vertical spinner (twin vertical bar, sometimes called a drum, about 120mph tip speed) between hinged forks/wedges. The old jaws stayed as an option but were rarely used. WC IV: heavier weapon, narrower forks, and the bar moved forward for better bite. WC V: optional 45lb single disk. WC VI-VII: invert wheels on the outside of the 'ears', name painted on the forks, Screw Job minibot (WC VI-VII) and Spitfire drone (WC VII).

weaponSpecs.notes: 120mph tip speed and two impactors refer to the WC III twin vertical bar. A 45lb single disk was an option from WC V. Jaw-era details (3hp motors, AutomationDirect 25:1 gearboxes, 250:1 total ratio) apply to WC I-II.

drive.selfRighting: none (invertible: 'ears' with wheels let it drive upside down)
drive.motors: 4x AmpFlow A28-250

materials: polycarbonate top armor (Bounty Hunters vs Beta)
armor.chassisShape: Compact low body with a central vertical spinner, hinged forks on each side of it, and raised side 'ears' with small wheels for driving inverted.

name: Hydra

debutSeason.notes: Replaced the retired Warrior series. Team Whyachi's Son of Whyachi won the Comedy Central-era heavyweight championship in its debut season. Hydra fought WC IV-VII.

weaponDescription: Front-mounted, rear-hinged flipping arm with a custom hydraulic system, the first hydraulic flipper in BattleBots. It builds up pressure in what Jake Ewert called 'pretty much a big spring'; releasing the spring pushes hydraulic fluid into the cylinder for a sudden throw, then the arm retracts. Test videos showed it launching a 450lb quad bike and a van. WC V: redesigned front end and internals; a 28lb steel 'Hydragate' corral attachment against HUGE. WC VI: rebuilt, with fluid filters and liquid cooling; full pressure in 4s (was 8s); cow-catcher dropped after a rule change. A vertical-spinner attachment was teased but never used. WC VII: 3/16in AR500 top plate added vs SawBlaze.

weaponSpecs.notes: spinUpTimeS is the time to recharge to full pressure (4s in WC VI; 8s before). No pressure or force figures are published. Records: about a 20ft flip on DeathRoll (brushed the rafters) and 20 flips on Free Shipping in one fight (both WC VII).

name: Bronco

debutSeason.notes: Inertia Labs built Comedy Central-era Toro (super heavyweight champion), The Matador and T-Minus. The original Bronco's flipper arm was a spare from The Matador. Fought WC I-IV plus Bounty Hunters; now runs only in Destruct-A-Thon live shows (donated 2023).

weaponDescription: Big pneumatic rear-hinged flipping arm (launcher), said to have almost three times the power of Toro. WC I: original four-wheel box, elongated flipper option vs Tombstone. WC II: two builds; the new one was longer with six wheels, plus armor options (angled rear wedge vs horizontal spinners, top guards vs axes/hammers). WC III: back to 4WD, launcher about 30% stronger than 2016, interchangeable 'pwanger' side armor vs vertical spinners, extra top armor vs overhead weapons. WC IV: largely unchanged, new rubber wheels and front wedgelets.

weaponSpecs.notes: battlebots.com fun fact: 'Bronco has 5 lbs of air on board'. No official psi, gas or energy figures were found. A 700lbf figure on a user-uploaded SketchUp model was rejected as unreliable.

name: Blacksmith

debutSeason.notes: Al Kindle entered Comedy Central Season 2.0 with lightweight Enforcer and an earlier version at 1996 US Robot Wars. Blacksmith fought WC II, III, IV and VI plus BattleBots: Champions I; it skipped WC V and WC VII. Inspired by Kindle's 30lb robot Mangi.

weaponDescription: Overhead electric hammer with a propane flamethrower built into the hammerhead (the 'flamethrower hammer'); it doubles as the self-righter. Driven by an NPC Black Max motor, aimed at fast, repeated, reliable hits rather than one-shot KOs. WC III: 13lb hammerhead, arm and head cut from one piece of AR500, machined titanium shaft, full swing arc in about 3s, enough torque to lift 250lb at the tip. WC IV: bulkier rounded head with a radioactive-symbol cutout, hardest-hitting version; overheating solved; the flame could burn 2+ minutes. WC VI-Champions I: hammer replaced by a 'power hammer' (green asymmetric hammer-saw disk on a chain-driven arm), with the flamethrower still at the back of the weapon axle.

weaponSpecs.forceOrPressure: enough torque to lift 250lb at the hammer tip (Al Kindle)
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb (13lb head) and spinUpTimeS (3s full swing arc) are the WC III hammer, from Al Kindle's Reddit AMA. WC VI hammer-saw disk specs aren't published. Fuel: propane.

name: HUGE

debutSeason.notes: No classic-era history. Competed in every season WC III to WC VII, plus Bounty Hunters (2020), Champions I (2021) and the 2026 Pro League. First reboot heavyweight from Connecticut.

weaponDescription: A big vertical spinning bar mounted high in the middle of the narrow body, so it hits opponents from above. The team brings several interchangeable bars: a longer bar for reach (used vs Bite Force in 2018), a shorter bar, a lighter I-shaped blade (WC VII final vs SawBlaze) and a heaviest blade (vs Minotaur, 2026). WC VI added two extra Maytech 4045 brushless motors so the bar reaches top speed faster, which had been a problem in earlier seasons. Driven by belts (in the WC VII final SawBlaze snapped two of them). When HUGE is upside down the bar spins downward instead of up.

Two huge flat white UHMW disc wheels (about 40 in across, about 1.5-2 in thick) at each end, each with two rings of six oval/teardrop cutouts forming spokes and a solid outer rim. Between them is a long, thin, square-section white box body sitting at hub height, only about 1/8 of the wheel diameter tall, with bolt holes and black pinstripe joints. A bare steel axle rod sticks out past each wheel's hub (the anti-side-stuck extension). On the body either side of the bar are two angry blue 'eye' brackets (navy crescents with a pupil) facing forward, added WC IV. Under the body two white legs splay down in an X/V to the floor as stabilizers. Optional black Tegris wheels replace the white ones (WC V on, used in the WC VII final). Semi-final. HUGE snapped Copperhead's right drive chain in the fourth weapon-on-weapon exchange, kept hitting it until the eggbeater smoked and stopped, then gyro-danced on one wheel while Copperhead was counted out and destroyed its snake minibot.

appearance.features: Angry-toddler theme. A squat, wide, bright-orange body with thin black outline stripes along every edge and bevel. The front is split by a central channel. Two raised orange pods on either side each carry one big cartoon angry eye (white eyeball, black pupil, black angled brow), so together they look like a scowling face. In the channel sits a short, fat bronze/dark-steel drum on a black sliding carriage with exposed rails, chains and black machinery behind it. On top of each pod is a chunky silver clenched fist on a self-righting arm, the left/right 'tantrum fists' (black-and-orange striped forearms). Two long black forks (or a hinged black-edged orange wedge) stick out in front of the pods. The TANTRUM logo is hand-lettered in black on the top-left pod. WC VII has small purple and green triangle panels on the black rear top deck and a SolidWorks decal on the side. The WC III original was a 4-wheel orange box with a titanium flipper lid, decorative fists and servo 'eyebrows'.

famousFights.summary: Giant Nut final. An early fork contact peeled Witch Doctor's baseplate down and high-centered it. Dillon Carey shoved it into the screws, punched off pieces of its armor and chewed a wheel. Witch Doctor could only drive in arcs and was counted out with about 30 seconds left.

Round of 16 comeback. Tantrum punched ROTATOR onto the Upper Deck, then got stuck when a snapped self-righter chain high-centered it and took heavy hits. It recovered, pinned ROTATOR with the drum spinning, peeled its front armor and finally rammed it out of the arena.

name: Son of Whyachi

builders.captain: Terry Ewert and Luke Ewert (co-captains in the reboot; Luke drove; battlebots.com 2019 lists Luke Ewert as builder)

debutSeason.notes: Classic-era debut Season 3.0 (Comedy Central, filmed May 2001, San Francisco), where it won the heavyweight Giant Nut as a 315 lb shufflebot (walking-beam drive got a walker weight bonus). Also entered Seasons 4.0 and 5.0 (superheavyweight) and the 2004 NPC Charity Open as tracked 'Nitro SOW'. Rebuilt at 250 lb, wheeled and LiPo-powered for the reboot: WC II (2016), WC III (2018), WC IV (2019), and Bounty Hunters (2020) as a bounty boss. Retired after that.

weaponDescription: The 'Cage of Death': a three-armed horizontal rotor (Terry Ewert calls it a 'cage spinner') whose arm tips are joined by red support tubes into a triangle, with heavy S7 tool steel hammers at each tip mounted low to the floor. It covers the whole robot and acts as its defense; the robot carries basically no armor. Classic Season 3.0: about 5 ft across, 120 lb rotor, three Etek motors, 390 rpm, 'over 70 mph' (Bill Nye). Reboot: mounted lower; toned down to 150 mph for WC III; WC IV got new 10 lb S7 hammers, faster spin-up and a 190 mph top speed, with the 120 lb rotor driven by eight Magmotors. Hammers were redesigned again for Bounty Hunters.

weaponSpecs.notes: Mixed eras, so read carefully: 120 lb rotor and 190 mph are WC IV (2019). 390 rpm and 5 ft (60 in) diameter are the classic Season 3.0 machine. Reboot rotor diameter and rpm not published. WC III was capped at 150 mph. Hammers: 10 lb each in WC IV, 10-12 lb in Season 3.0.

drive.selfRighting: none. Its known weakness, though it was only flipped four times in its career (Bounty Hunter, Brutus, Whiplash, Gigabyte)
drive.motors: 4x Astro 90 Cobalt motors (reboot; various 4S and 5S LiPo). Classic: 4 mph walking-beam shufflebot (S3.0-4.0), six-wheel drive (S5.0), tracks (2004)

appearance.features: Reboot look (WC IV): a flat, low, bare-metal (brushed aluminum/silver) square chassis, close to the floor, with a wide grey steel wedge plate across the front. On top is a giant three-armed rotor that covers the whole bot and overhangs the chassis on every side. Three thick gloss-black box-section arms 120 degrees apart meet at a central steel hub (bolts, red hub accents). Each arm tip carries a chunky black hammer block hanging down close to the floor with a small red Whyachi triangle logo. Thin glossy red round tubes run tip to tip and form an equilateral triangle (the 'cage'). Chassis decals: big red 'WHYACHI' script with 'Son of' above, and black/white 'UDDER GUN' and VEX Robotics sponsor stickers (TKO stickers for Bounty Hunters). Wheels are hidden under the chassis. Low-poly tip: flat box plus wedge, three long black prisms from a cylinder hub, three red thin cylinders joining the tips, three hammer blocks.

giantNutWins.event: Season 3.0 heavyweight championship (CLASSIC Comedy Central era, not the reboot). Beat BioHazard in the final.

notableRecords: Classic era: first heavyweight champion of a televised BattleBots event with a horizontal spinner, first shufflebot champion, and one of only two bots (with Bite Force) to win a championship in their debut season
Only robot to go undefeated against BioHazard
Reboot best: Round of 16 in WC III (#8 seed) and WC IV (#10 seed). WC II: #6 seed, lost in Round of 32
All-time record per wiki: 18 wins, 10 losses

famousFights.summary: Heavyweight Giant Nut final. The cage tore off BioHazard's skirts and threw it across the BattleBox. BioHazard pushed SOW into the pulverizer and nearly flipped it, but SOW then wrecked BioHazard's right-side drive. BioHazard was first counted out, but because it could still move on one side with 10 seconds left, the result was changed to a judges' decision, and the crowd booed.
Fight Night 4. A weapon clash with the future champion sent SOW flying into the Lexan and onto the screw mount, but End Game was left immobile and counted out. That earned SOW a Top 16 spot.
Fight Night 1. After a few even exchanges SOW tore part of HUGE's left wheel off, and a follow-up hit left HUGE unable to move and counted out.

trivia: 'Whyachi' is a word made up in the team's shop that means 'to bring someone down hard and inflict massive amounts of pain or damage'.

WC V added faster-spin-up pulleys, a belt guard and black paint on the weapon, plus optional add-ons (magnets for downforce, an extra top section with hammers, a welded-in AR500 bar for horizontal spinners). WC VII ran 140 mph on purpose for more 'bite'. Flipping over doesn't stop it fighting because the drum works either way up.

appearance.features: Snake theme (copperhead viper). Across the front, between the wheels, is a wide dark gunmetal drum with two big rounded-rectangle pocket cutouts and a steel shaft showing at the ends. The frame and drum mounts are weathered rusty copper/bronze. The top plate is glossy red painted with a snake-scale pattern of dark bronze hexagons outlined in black and yellow, with a round team logo in the center and big hex bolt heads. At each front corner a low angled 'fang' wedge sticks forward, painted black with red/yellow scale stripes and a bare-steel ground edge. On the right a row of red-tipped spikes fans out like a snake rattle/ribs. A 2026 recolor is black and copper (outside the 2015-23 window). It's often joined by orange four-wheeled minibots with snake heads and tails.

famousFights.summary: Fight Night 1, with an AR500 bar welded on to fight spinners. The first hit knocked off Gigabyte's self-righting stick, and a later huge hit sent Gigabyte's shell up to the BattleBox ceiling, breaking a light, while Gigabyte landed upside down and was counted out.

Copperhead split one end of Riptide's eggbeater and flipped it, then broke its own right axle late on. Team Break32 appealed, and judge Derek Young re-scored Aggression, which made the decision unanimous.

others: Alex Espinosa (WC III, Bounty Hunters-WC VI)

debutSeason.notes: Before the reboot, a 120 lb middleweight Icewave (called 'Goliath' at BattleBots IQ 2004) fought BattleBots IQ 2004-2006, the 2004 NPC Charity Open, Cisco Party 2006 and JavaOne 2007, winning the BattleBots IQ 2005 120 lb college division. These were not Comedy Central TV seasons. Reboot: WC I, II, III, Bounty Hunters (2020, bounty boss) and WC VI. Skipped WC IV and V, wasn't selected for WC VII, then retired as a Destruct-A-Thon display.

weaponDescription: A 54 in, 47 lb steel horizontal bar spinning on top of the robot, mounted slightly forward of center, powered by a 15 hp internal combustion engine (the 'ICE' in Icewave) adapted from a Husqvarna concrete saw. The engine sits in a housing above the bar and runs on 100-octane fuel. Early tip speed was claimed at up to 300 mph, later limited by the 250 mph rule from WC III, and actually capped at 200 mph for safety in WC III. A shorter bar exists for stability (used vs Vanquish). The bar tips are painted to blend with the floor so opponents misjudge its reach. WC VI: new engine layout with key parts moved back, and a fully independent weapon system with its own 100Ah battery and controllers for the starter motor. The team brought five blades.

weaponSpecs.motor: 15 hp internal combustion engine modified from a Husqvarna concrete saw (100-octane fuel)
weaponSpecs.notes: 200 mph is the WC III safety cap. Earlier seasons were cited at up to 300 mph. The 54 in bar was once the longest weapon in robot combat (since passed by Mammoth). teethOrImpactors = two bar tips.

drive.selfRighting: one-shot self-righting mechanism on the left side of the engine cover added in WC II. Otherwise it relies on staying upright
drive.motors: 2x Magmotors (power: 2x 6S 5Ah LiPo for drive)

materials: steel front plow (reinforced for WC VI)
metal flat chassis with clear polycarbonate top panels
armor.chassisShape: Low, flat, square chassis with a full-width angled front plow. The engine housing sits on top, with the bar spinning between housing and chassis
armor.dimensionsIn: bar 54 in long; chassis dimensions not published

appearance.features: WC I-III look: a low, flat, square silver/bare-metal chassis (machined frame, clear polycarbonate top panels showing the internals). A full-width navy-blue front plow wedge angles down to the floor with 'ICEWAVE' in yellow block letters. On top, set slightly forward of center, is a tall octagonal engine housing: navy-blue lower sides (SolidWorks and Big Blue Saw decals), a golden-yellow faceted top cap (yellow from WC III) with ICEWAVE lettering, and a short black exhaust/intake tube sticking up at an angle. Just under the housing, the long flat bar spins horizontally a few inches above the chassis, reaching about 1.5x the chassis width. It is black with a red-orange stripe down the middle and grey tips painted to hide its length. WC VI and Bounty Hunters recolor: the plow and housing are matte black with yellow (#F2E340) accents and black lettering, with blue triangles on the housing edges. Optional three wedgelets on the plow in WC VI. Low-poly tip: flat box, wedge prism in front, octagonal prism housing on top, long flat bar plank between them.

otherAwards: BattleBots IQ 2005 120 lb College Division Champion (pre-reboot middleweight version)
notableRecords: #2 seed in WC I, the only top-4 seed that year not to reach the semi-finals
Split Vanquish in half (WC III) and tore HUGE down the middle (WC III)
Its 54 in bar was once the longest weapon in robot combat
One of only three robots (with Bronco and Son of Whyachi) to fight in Bounty Hunters only that year

famousFights.summary: Fight Night 1, with the shorter bar for stability. Icewave shredded Vanquish's rear treads, then one huge strike to the side of the plow tore the frame in two, leaving the left drive and plow several feet from the rest of the robot.
Fight Night 4 with a Top 16 spot on the line. The first hit tore into a HUGE wheel, and the third ripped HUGE down the middle so it collapsed and was counted out.

Quarter-final, and what Chris Rose called the biggest upset of the tournament. Ghost Raptor gripped the engine housing with a special 'de-icer' attachment, Icewave's own hit on its plow flipped Icewave upside down, and Ghost Raptor pinned it against the screws until it was counted out.

trivia: Icewave's engine comes from a Husqvarna concrete saw and burns 100-octane fuel. Kenny Florian called it 'the '69 Camaro of bots'.

name: DUCK!

others: Kathy Rucker (WC III, WC VI-Champions I)

hometown: Palo Alto, CA (battlebots.com 2021 and wiki; battlebots.com 2018 lists Hillsborough, CA)

debutSeason.notes: An upgraded version of Hal Rucker's RoboGames 2015/2017 heavyweight 'Whoops!' (which beat Last Rites/Tombstone at RoboGames 2017). The Ruckers had entered WC II with The Ringmaster. Competed WC III, WC IV and WC VI. Accepted for WC V but withdrew because of COVID delays. Last fights in Champions I (2021), then retired.

weaponDescription: A steel lifting 'beak'/plow worked by Hannah Rucker. WC III: a wide white wedge plow in front of the front wheels with an orange chisel-shaped beak in the center to get under opponents. WC IV ('DUCK! 2.0'): new 50 lb, 3/4 in steel beak on support arms mounted between the wheels. It could rotate a full 360 degrees, protected the front wheels when lowered, and had a sharp black tip on top that doubled as an overhead axe. It had so much torque it could flip its own chassis. WC V design (not fought) and WC VI: internally mounted arms and a narrower, more traditional wedge-shaped lifter about a quarter of the bot's width. In WC VI the beak split down the middle to open like a real duck bill, with speakers that quack as it opens. Interchangeable wedges, hinged forks or a big defensive plow (the plow cost two drive motors to make weight). It does almost no damage, so it fights by control.

weaponSpecs.notes: 50 lb, 3/4 in steel is the WC IV beak/plow. Lift actuator, motor and force are not published.

drive.selfRighting: none (invertible; the 360-degree beak in WC IV could also right it)
drive.motors: 4x Maytech 65162 brushless (WC VI). Power: 4x MaxAmps 4Ah 37V 150C LiPo. 7 in Brazil wheels on all four corners from WC IV; harder vulcanized rubber wheels in WC VI

materials: unibody milled from one 6061 aluminum billet (WC III, per battlebots.com 2018)
magnesium billet unibody (WC VI, per battlebots.com 2021)
armor.chassisShape: Very low, flat, rectangular box (invertible), wheels at the four corners, beak in a central front slot

appearance.features: Rubber-duck theme. A very low, flat, rectangular white/light-grey slab (about as tall as its wheels), covered in a grid of small black countersunk bolt holes. Four black rubber wheels are fully exposed in cut-outs at the four corners (orange hubs in WC III). WC III: a wide flat white wedge plow across the whole front, with a small orange chisel-shaped 'beak' (with two nostril holes) sticking out of its middle. The top plate says 'DUCK!' in big orange letters, with a blue circle containing a cartoon yellow/orange duck face and a blue Protolabs logo. WC VI: the body splits into two long white side pods with rows of rounded vent slots on the sides, and a central slot at the front holding a bright orange split duck-bill lifter that opens up and down. A teal panel with the cartoon duck face sits on top between the pods, plus orange/teal dot decals and Protolabs branding on the sides. WC IV: a big rotating beak on side arms with a sharp black axe tip above the 'face'. Low-poly tip: flat box, four corner cylinders, orange wedge/beak in a front notch.

notableRecords: Became a WC III fan favorite after winning its debut three-way rumble
Known for durability: survived almost three minutes against Tombstone, losing only after driving over the killsaws on its last wheel
Never made a World Championship tournament bracket
Competitive record per wiki: 5 wins, 8 losses

famousFights.summary: The reigning champion took both sides of DUCK!'s plow and three of its wheels, but DUCK! kept coming, and Tombstone's bent frame slowed its own weapon until Tombstone froze. DUCK! looked like it would win, but its last wheel quit after driving over the killsaws, and it was counted out while Tombstone came back to life.

Revenge for the controversial 2018 Last Chance Rumble. DUCK! got a lift near the barrier and flipped Bombshell over, and Bombshell couldn't self-right with its disk. Hal Rucker later said production wanted him to flip Bombshell back to make the fight last longer.

Debut three-way rumble. Mecha Rampage tore off a DUCK! wheel, but DUCK! pinned Mecha Rampage against the wall, lifted and overturned Free Shipping, and pushed it into the screws while Mecha Rampage burned.

trivia: The WC VI beak splits open like a real duck's bill and plays a quack through built-in speakers. The original DUCK! was built in just 28 days.
uncertain: armor.materials (wiki contradicts itself on WC III aluminum vs magnesium; battlebots.com says aluminum 2018, magnesium 2021)

name: Bloodsport

debutSeason.notes: No classic-era history. Started as a reserve in 2019 and was called into the main competition; the first version was built in seven weeks. Total rebuild ('v3') for WC VII.

weaponDescription: Overhead horizontal spinner: the blade spins above the low chassis. WC IV: round black/red bot with a 47" S7 tool steel bar with blood-spattered edges. WC V: new low box chassis inspired by the team's beetleweight Zero Traction, four hinged front wedgelets and five swappable weapons (Long Bar, The Disk, Tri-bar, THICC bar, the Key), 57-77 lb, made of AR500 and S7; the THICC bar beat End Game. WC VI: all-AR500 weapons (heaviest 72 lb) after S7 blades snapped, plus the 'Club Sandwich'. Champions I: 'Ferrous Wheel' disk. WC VII (v3): weapon electronics moved into a 'head' housing above the blade, new 75 lb 'Chonk Key' (1.25" AR500), 68 lb twin-tooth 'Wheel of Misfortune' and the 72 lb 'Long Bar'.

weaponSpecs.motor: 4x Scorpion 5025 (WC V); twin Newmotor 8025 before FaceOffs
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb is the WC VII 'Long Bar' (72 lb). Other WC VII options: Chonk Key 75 lb, Wheel of Misfortune 68 lb. lengthOrDiameterIn 47 is the WC IV bar. tipSpeedMph 250 is the BattleBots maximum, which the wiki says the WC V weapon motors could reach. teethOrImpactors 2 = bar ends (the WC VI tri-bar has 3; a four-toothed bar was also used).

drive.selfRighting: Curved pole on top of the weapon head: weapon torque rolls the bot over the pole. It cannot self-right without the weapon (this lost it fights to Lock-Jaw and MadCatter).
drive.motors: 4x short Magmotors (WC IV-VI), replaced by TP brushless motors for WC VII

armor.chassisShape: WC IV: round, about 32" across. WC V onward: low, flat, box-shaped chassis with hinged front wedgelets. WC VII: compact single-billet frame with the weapon head on top.

appearance.features: WC VII (v3) model: very low, flat, near-square matte black slab chassis, about 2 ft each way, with chamfered corners and exposed bolt heads. Four red treaded wheels sit inside cut-outs in the side rails, two per side. Four separate hinged wedgelets hang off the front edge, each a short downward-angled tongue in red with black splatter. A raised black 'head' sits in the centre on a large exposed silver gear ring. The head is a rounded wedge housing with a serrated, sawtooth top ridge and two angry, angular red eyes on the front face. A thick curved black tube rises from the head's top and bends into a shepherd's-crook hook: the self-righting pole. The bar spins horizontally just below the head and well above the chassis. It is long and red with dark blood-splatter texture and stretches well past the chassis on both sides. 'BLOODSPORT' is written in red graffiti on the side rails. WC IV look (alternate): round black and red body with the bar on top. Proving Ground 2023: chassis and head repainted white.

notableRecords: First bot to beat an eventual Giant Nut winner in the same season (KO of End Game, WC V 2020); End Game's only loss that year
Unbeaten 3-0 in WC V Fight Nights; No.2 seed for the 2020 tournament
First robot immobilized on the Upper Deck hazard

famousFights.summary: Main Event. Running the THICC bar, Bloodsport lost its wedgelets early and was thrown into a corner, but End Game's drive failed and it lost its weapon belt while smoking. End Game was counted out; it was the champion's only defeat of the season.

Main Event. The 72 lb Long Bar sent ROTATOR into a 360-degree aerial spin and bent its wheelguard. Bloodsport got hung up on an Upper Deck screw, broke free, then wrecked ROTATOR's left drive and weapon.

Round of 32 revenge attempt. Bloodsport shredded Lock-Jaw's tires and tore off its right-front wheel, briefly catching fire in the process. Then it flipped itself on a big hit to Lock-Jaw's spinner and its weapon died, so it couldn't self-right. Marple blamed himself afterwards.

trivia: Its debut-season self-righting pole was borrowed from Gigabyte's team (Robotic Death Company).

name: Beta

debutSeason.notes: Entered Comedy Central Season 5.0 (2002) but withdrew: its magnets pulled up the Test Box floor panels. Accepted for WC I (2015) but forfeited after an airline lost a 25 kg bag of parts. First fought in WC II. John Reid also built the Robot Wars hammer bots Terrorhurtz and KillerHurtz.

weaponDescription: Overhead hammer that strikes the top of opponents and doubles as the self-righter. WC II: electric hammer on a long, bent arm (bent so it can hit opponents mid-air). WC V: switched to a shorter, nitrogen-powered pneumatic hammer, which Reid says is lighter and about three times as powerful. WC VII: a new 16 lb bladed hammer made from 10 mm AR500, inspired by Jason Marston's robot Thor, alongside the classic hammer head (the 'skinny' blade weighs the same).

weaponSpecs.actuator: Electric (WC II); pneumatic, nitrogen-powered (WC V onward)
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb is the WC VII bladed hammer (16 lb, 10 mm AR500), which weighs the same as the classic head. Beta's pre-reboot 2002 build had an 11 kg (~24 lb) aluminum hammer head; that isn't the reboot spec.

drive.selfRighting: Hammer arm swings over to flip it back up
drive.motors: 2x 48V Bosch DC (WC I to Bounty Hunters); 2x Maytech 6880 brushless (WC VII, saving just over 14 lb)

materials: polycarbonate top (8 mm, WC I build)
armor.chassisShape: Low, wide trapezoid with sloped plow armor wrapping the front and sides. The hammer pivots near the rear-centre and lands over the nose.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a squat, wide wedge of raw, dark, unpainted welded steel plate. The base is a broad trapezoid whose front and side plow panels slope outward and down to the floor, like an upturned tray with the top open. Inside, exposed internals (pneumatic tank, wiring) sit under clear panels. A polished aluminum truss-style hammer arm, triangular cut-outs along its length, rises from a pivot near the back. At rest it angles up and backwards, ending in a chunky cylindrical steel hammer head; for the alternate WC VII model, swap the head for a flat AR500 blade. An orange top plate at the rear carries a large white Greek letter beta (β) logo. The wheels are mostly hidden inside the armor skirt.

notableRecords: WC II quarter-finalist (2016)
Unbeaten 3-0 in WC V Fight Nights
Bounty boss in BattleBots: Bounty Hunters (lost its bounty to Lock-Jaw)
Team Hurtz were the only British team to attend all of the first seven televised seasons

famousFights.summary: Quarter-final against the No.1 seed. Beta tanked Tombstone's hits with its plow, drove it into the wall so it landed upside-down, and pinned it. Tombstone eventually ripped Beta's hammer arm away from its housing. It was a back-and-forth fight that went the distance.

Running a lighter hammer and thicker armor, Beta mostly pushed ROTATOR into the screws and lost its hammer head on ROTATOR's disk. A controversial win for a bot that barely used its weapon; it pushed the producers to update the judging guidelines.

Seeding decider between two 2-1 bots. Beta controlled the whole fight, repeatedly shoving Bloodsport into the screws and Upper Deck, and hammered its weapon head until the front casing was hacked apart.

trivia: Beta is pronounced 'bee-tah', British style.

name: Quantum

debutSeason.notes: Withdrew from WC V (COVID travel) and skipped WC VI; returned fully rebuilt for WC VII, keeping only the drive motors and hydraulics. No classic-era history. Named after the Bond film 'Quantum of Solace'; its sister bot for Chinese events is Spectre.

weaponDescription: Hydraulic crushing beak/jaw with swappable teeth: a twin-fang head, or a single tooth for maximum crushing pressure against non-spinners. The hydraulic system snaps the jaw shut fast to grab, then changes pressure to crush. The WC VII head was much stronger and could crush harder than the 2019 one. A rear self-righting arm, like Witch Doctor's or HyperShock's, doubles as a victory salute.

weaponSpecs.forceOrPressure: 35,000 lbf at the tip, over 50,000 lbf toward the back of the jaw
weaponSpecs.notes: Force figures are from the wiki's general description. Teeth: 2 (twin fangs) by default; a single-tooth beak was also used (vs Valkyrie WC IV, Gruff WC VII).

drive.selfRighting: Rear self-righting arm (srimech)
drive.motors: 4x brushed LEM motors, chosen over brushless for precise control; 14S LiPo

materials: HARDOX steel front wedge (4-6 mm, shock/rubber mounted)
armor.chassisShape: Sleek, low 4WD body with an angular layered front wedge/plow; the crushing head sits on top and the srimech is at the rear.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a sports-car-like body. The rear half is glossy royal blue with sharp, faceted panels and 'Quantum' in thin white lettering on the sides. Blue-hubbed wheels poke out at the rear corners, and a small grille vent sits behind the rear wheel. The front half is a dark gunmetal/black wedge built from layered, angular plates that sweep low to the floor in a broad plow. Mounted on top is a large polished-silver skeletal head shaped like an animal skull or beak, with organic cut-outs. It is hinged at the back and opens upward. Its front edge carries long, curved black fangs and a row of smaller serrated teeth, so it looks like an open-mouthed beast. 3D-printed 'quill' hairs were added in WC VII for a more sinister look. The srimech arm folds flat at the rear.

otherAwards: Best Design Award (World Championship IV, 2019)
notableRecords: First WC VII bot to finish 4-0 in Fight Nights; No.5 seed
One of the heaviest modern bots still under 250 lb; in 2019 a few coins would have put it overweight

famousFights.summary: Play-in for the Top 16. Valkyrie flipped itself with its own gyroscopic forces. Quantum lost its single tooth but still grabbed Valkyrie, paraded it, and parked it in the gap behind the screws where it couldn't escape.

Comeback fight after two seasons away. Quantum box-rushed the shell spinner and bit through its UHMW cover and frame again and again, carrying it to the pulverizer and the screws until fire erupted inside.

Round of 32 as the No.5 seed. Ribbot got stuck in the killsaw slots early and Quantum sportingly held back. Once free, Ribbot used its forks and disk to flip Quantum twice, separating the crusher head from its hydraulic ram. Quantum couldn't self-right.

trivia: Quantum is the only heavyweight to have competed with a name starting with Q.

name: ROTATOR

debutSeason.notes: Inspired by Victor Soto's middleweight Blue Flame. Was an alternate in 2016 and got in because of drop-outs. Officially styled ROTATOЯ with a reversed R; also written ROTATOR or RotatoR.

weaponDescription: WC II-IV: twin horizontal spinners, one above the chassis (overcutter) and one below (undercutter), so it looked the same when flipped, like its palindromic name. Each disk was 30 lb at 300 mph in 2016. WC III: option to drop one disk for a thicker titanium plow and wheelguards. WC IV: swappable 20 lb bars and hinged rear forks; 2019 was the last time the double-disk setup was used. WC V onward: a single low horizontal spinner (disk or bar, a 40 lb bar is mentioned), with a plow or wedgelets for defence.

weaponSpecs.notes: massLb 30 and tipSpeedMph 300 are the per-disk figures for the WC II (2016) twin-disk version. Later single weapons: 20 lb bars (WC IV) and a 40 lb bar. No later RPM or tip-speed figures found.

drive.selfRighting: none (invertible)

armor.chassisShape: Low, flat, roughly hexagonal invertible body. Large tires stand taller than the chassis at the rear, and the wiki mentions a castor. An angled plow, hinged forks or wedgelets bolt on.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a low, flat, black, roughly hexagonal slab, wide at the back and tapering to an angled front plow. Two big grey knobbly pneumatic tires stick out past the top and bottom of the rear corners, which is what makes it invertible. A broad stripe of shiny mirror-gold runs front to back on the top deck. Gold chrome panels with 'ROTATOR' in stencil-style black letters (last R reversed) wrap the angled front plow. A large flat black undercutter disk/bar sits under the front, sticking well out past the plow and sides; its two tooth ends are gold-tipped. Small orange LEDs sit near the castor (from WC V). Matte gold in early seasons; shiny gold with the name and logo on top since WC VI.

otherAwards: Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship III, 2018)
Bounty Hunters bounty winner: took Bronco's bounty (BattleBots: Bounty Hunters, 2021)
notableRecords: Only robot to go the distance with eventual champion End Game in 2020
First robot to have fought every World Champion (achieved by WC VI)
Until WC VII, lost to the eventual champion every time it made the tournament

famousFights.summary: Main Event upset. Fitted with the plow that beat Icewave, ROTATOR's first hit sent Tombstone flying and chipped its bar. Tombstone began smoking, its weapon spun down, and it eventually caught fire and stopped.
Round of 16 grudge match against the No.6 seed. ROTATOR tanked early hits until Icewave's combustion engine stalled, then tore the engine housing apart and took out the engine itself.
Bounty match after beating Axolotl, Captain Shrederator and MadCatter. ROTATOR tore into Bronco's wedge, broke its flipper pin and ripped off a wheelguard, surviving several pulverizer hits.
famousFights.result: Won by JD; claimed the Bronco bounty ($25,000)

trivia: A 2016 video suggests ROTATOR was originally meant to have a flamethrower.

name: Valkyrie
team: Team VALKYRIE (Team Questionable Designs, WC III-V)

builders.captain: Leanne Cushing (Lucy Du captained and drove in WC VII and Champions II)

debutSeason.notes: No classic-era history. Listed as Cambridge, MA in WC III, Somerville, MA from WC IV to Champions II, and Berkeley, CA from FaceOffs on.

weaponDescription: Low undercutting horizontal spinner on a two-wheel, V-shaped chassis. It has a big arsenal of named weapons. WC III: 'Dr. Tooth' (two-tooth disk), 'Sonic the Wedgehog' (six teeth) and the bar 'The Spirit of Boston'. WC IV: 65 lb, 1" AR500 bow-tie bar 'Sweet Caroline'. WC V: 'Sour Caroline' (green-painted inside), the three-tooth 36" disk 'Glory', and 'Mr. Cavity'; weapon motor around 40 hp. WC VI: 'Dr. Acula' with bolted-on teeth. WC VII: new 65 lb 'Artemis' (single-tooth disk in the hero shots), plus an optional long hinged fork.

weaponSpecs.motor: Etek motor(s), around 40 hp (WC V); three sensored Castle brushless from FaceOffs 2024
weaponSpecs.notes: massLb 65 is both 'Sweet Caroline' (WC IV) and 'Artemis' (WC VII). lengthOrDiameterIn 36 is the 'Glory' disk (WC V). teethOrImpactors 1 is the WC VII hero-shot disk; other weapons have 2, 3 or 6 teeth.

drive.selfRighting: none (invertible)

materials: steel armor (black paint over blue primer, WC IV-VI)
armor.chassisShape: V-shaped (chevron) two-wheel body with the wheels at the outer rear corners and the undercutter at the front point.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a low chevron/arrowhead body, its point at the front, flaring back into two arms. Each arm ends at an outer rear corner with an exposed black treaded wheel that is taller than the body. Panels are deep navy blue with crisp white/silver angular stripe graphics and black trim, all edged with rows of black bolt heads. Two glowing blue LED 'eyes' sit just behind the nose. Under the front point is a large flat navy undercutter disk, almost as wide as the body. It has one big hooked, scythe-like tooth and a large cut-out window. Pre-WC VII look (WC IV-VI): mostly black with blue accents and blue primer underneath, so it 'bleeds blue' when scraped.

otherAwards: Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship V, 2020)
notableRecords: First Round of 16 run in WC V (2020)
Champions II Sin City Slugfest runner-up (lost the final to SHREDDIT BRO!)
On the losing end of the first televised Appeal in BattleBots history (vs Malice, WC VII)
Never lost an exhibition fight
Lucy Du was the only female driver who also captained a team in the WC VII field

famousFights.summary: Undercutter vs undercutter. With the three-tooth 'Glory' disk, Valkyrie sheared rubber off ROTATOR's tire and late on tore away its wedge and left wheelguard. Both weapons were dead at the end, and the judges inspected both robots.
Round of 32 as the No.9 seed. After bouncing off the Lexan, Valkyrie ripped off SubZero's rear plow and front wedges and killed half its drive. Valkyrie's first win in the championship bracket.

Malice stripped the threads holding the 'Glory' disk, which flew off and flipped Valkyrie. Both bots then limped around with drive problems. Valkyrie first got a split decision, but Malice's Appeal (the first ever televised) had the judges rescore it.
famousFights.result: Lost by JD (unanimous on appeal; originally a split decision for Valkyrie)

trivia: Valkyrie is one of the few robots whose team and announcer Faruq Tauheed call it 'she'.

name: Cobalt
team: Robotic Death Company (WC VI onward; originally Team Carbide, WC II and WC IV)

builders.captain: John Mladenik (WC VII era); Matt Olson captain and driver from FaceOffs 2024
others: Dave Moulds (original builder; drove in WC VII)

debutSeason.notes: Built by British engineers Dave Moulds and Sam Smith, who also built Robot Wars Series 9 champion Carbide. Skipped WC III (filming clash with China's 'This is Fighting Robots') and WC V (COVID travel). Handed to Robotic Death Company for WC VI when Moulds and Smith briefly retired; they rejoined for WC VII. The first modern bot entered by both a UK and a US team.

weaponDescription: WC II (2016): invertible two-wheel bot with an asymmetrical horizontal bar spinner. WC IV onward: complete redesign into a four-wheel, steep-wedge bot with a toothed vertical spinning disk mounted at the front centre. Its WC IV wedge was too steep to get under opponents. WC VI: less steep wedge and a 36 lb disk decorated with gear patterns and a robot skull on the tooth, plus a 50 lb weapon option for vertical spinners. WC VII: 45 lb serrated disk 'Nasty' with bright green teeth (a 45 lb asymmetric disk was also used), usually with long hinged forks.

weaponSpecs.notes: massLb 45 is the WC VII 'Nasty' disk. Other options: 36 lb disk (WC VI), 50 lb anti-vertical weapon (WC VI). Teeth count not verified; the WC VII photo shows a many-toothed sprocket-like ring.

drive.selfRighting: No dedicated self-righter (WC IV build); relies on weapon/gyro forces. When it lost its weapon belt it couldn't self-right. Rear 'horns' added at FaceOffs 2024 let the disk partly spin while inverted.
drive.motors: Long Magmotors (WC VII era), replaced by 2x HyperDrive motors in 2026

armor.chassisShape: Steep, flat-sided wedge shaped like a truncated pyramid/hood, with a vertical disk slot in the front centre and twin hinged forks or wedgelets in front.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a glossy black body like a low truncated pyramid. Steep flat sloping panels fall to the floor on the front and sides, under a flat top deck with a raised black motor/belt housing toward the front. A large black vertical disk sits in a slot at the front centre, its top half well above the deck. Its rim is a ring of bright lime-green, sprocket-like serrated teeth, and a silver hub sits on a black shaft housing. Two long, thin, bright-green hinged forks angle down from either side of the disk to the floor, reaching well past the nose. A green 'COBALT' logo in a speed-line font is on the side panels, with small sponsor decals. The wheels are hidden inside the body. Alternate WC II (2016) look: white, blue and red invertible horizontal bar spinner.

otherAwards: Most Destructive Robot Award (World Championship IV, 2019)
notableRecords: WC VI quarter-finalist (2021), beating Yeti and Whiplash
Champions II Sin City Slugfest runner-up (lost to JackPot)
Has competed in every even-numbered reboot season, plus WC VII

famousFights.summary: Cobalt shredded both of Ghost Raptor's front wheels and flipped it. Then it charged its upturned opponent across the BattleBox into the wall by the drivers, splitting Ghost Raptor apart in a shower of sparks. Remembered as one of the most visceral knockouts in the show's history.

Round of 16 against the No.3 seed. Whiplash lifted Cobalt several times, then got a fork stuck in the Upper Deck and Cobalt pounded it. Cobalt got stuck on the arena floor and debris jammed its switch, so the referee called a double KO. The show implied Cobalt's spinner couldn't be shut off; the team disputes this.
famousFights.result: Won by split JD after a double KO

famousFights.summary: Quarter-final against the eventual champion. Tantrum peeled up Cobalt's forks, ground its drum on Cobalt's underside, and slammed it so hard that Cobalt, helped by its own disk, flew out of the arena.
famousFights.result: Lost by KO (out of the arena)

trivia: Even under the American Robotic Death Company, Cobalt sported the Union Jack in WC VI.

name: Gigabyte

builders.captain: John Mladenik (WC III-VI); Derek Tran and Camden Wallraff (WC VII)

debutSeason.notes: Successor to the team's classic-era superheavyweight shell spinner Megabyte, which fought in the superheavyweight class. Robotic Death Company also run Cobalt (WC VI onward).

weaponDescription: Full-body spinning shell with steel teeth on the rim. A curved self-righting pole sticks up through the middle of the shell; it also shows the driver which way the bot is facing. WC III: rainbow shell, 110 lb, on a cast-aluminum mast that broke against Tombstone. WC IV: bi-directional teeth, a rounded self-righting staff, a Lexan cover over the electronics, and a 130 lb heaviest shell. WC V: black shell with flames; D2 minibots when it had spare weight. WC VI: improved weapon motor, a shell designed for fighting verticals, and spring-loaded front forks. WC VII: brushless drive, teeth with two catching points per side, and four shells (two 0.25" AR500, one 0.1875" AR500, one 0.41" titanium with a flat lower edge).

weaponSpecs.motor: Brushed weapon motor (kept brushed in WC VII)
weaponSpecs.notes: Wiki gives a 120 lb shell (originally 110 lb; a 130 lb shell was built for WC IV). Tip speed sources disagree: 161 mph (quoted on the show), around 170 mph (debut season and the 'previous' figure before 2023), and 188 mph after upgrades at Proving Ground 2023. 170 mph is used for the 2018-2022 TV era. Teeth: two impactor blocks on opposite sides of the rim (WC VII photo).

drive.selfRighting: Curved pole sticking up through the centre of the shell
drive.motors: 2x short Magmotors (WC III-VI); 2x TP5680 brushless (WC VII, the same motors as Tantrum)

armor.chassisShape: Round, low, domed shell covering the whole robot, with the pole rising from the centre.

appearance.features: WC VII model: a wide, low, flat-topped dome, like a squat round cake tin about a third as tall as it is wide, in glossy black. Big white block letters spell 'GIGABYTE' around the side, with orange-and-yellow flame graphics licking up from the bottom edge. The flat top has a ring of eight trapezoid grey steel wear plates around a central silver hub. Two chunky steel tooth blocks bolted with brass bolts sit on opposite sides of the lower rim and stick out beyond it. A short shaft rises from the hub into a tall coral-red pole. The pole goes straight up, bends toward the back, and ends in a white rounded tip with a black dot, like an eye. A small black triangular fin sits on the rear of the top deck. The wheels are hidden under the shell. Alternate WC III look: rainbow-striped shell.

otherAwards: Bounty Hunters bounty winner: took Son of Whyachi's bounty (BattleBots: Bounty Hunters, 2021)
notableRecords: First Round of 16 appearance in WC V (2020)
Champions II Sin City Slugfest runner-up (lost to Free Shipping)
Survived the full three minutes with No.1 seed Hydra in 2020

famousFights.summary: Debut Main Event. Tombstone's third hit broke the shell retainer and its next blow tore the 110 lb shell clean off, leaving the electronics exposed. The team tried to tap out, but referee John Remar told them 'there's no tapping out', so they stopped driving to be counted out. The mast turned out to be cast aluminum instead of machined 6061.
Using its heaviest shell, Gigabyte kept spinning up and stayed on top of Minotaur so its drum couldn't reach full speed, chipping its front while losing a tooth itself.

Bounty match after beating GRABOT, Big Dill and Copperhead. Huge spinner collisions sent both bots flying and cost Gigabyte its pole. Son of Whyachi landed on top and flipped Gigabyte, but Gigabyte kept hitting until the bounty holder was counted out.
famousFights.result: Won by KO; claimed the Son of Whyachi bounty

trivia: For China's TV rules the team had to call itself 'Robotic Destruction Company', because 'death' can't be said on air there.
